meta.verification_method: Direct inspection of locally cloned repositories at pinned commit SHAs, cross-checked against resume PDFs and LinkedIn export. No claim is marked VERIFIED on the basis of a README, a resume line, or a generated description alone.

states.VERIFIED: Checked against primary source evidence (code, committed data file, or test) and the evidence supports the claim as worded.
states.VERIFICATION_REQUIRED: Plausible and self-reported but no public primary source exists. Typically employer-internal. Never stated as established fact.
states.UNSUPPORTED: Primary source evidence was inspected and does not support the claim as worded.
states.DEPRECATED: Previously made and since retracted or superseded.

sssd.name: SS-SD
sssd.author: team capstone; upstream commits authored by teammate

claims.claim: The silent-failure-detection framework is 8,209 lines of Python across 56 modules with 261 tests.
claims.verification_note: find . -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l gives 8209 total across 56 files; 261 functions match ^def test_ under tests/.

claims.claim: The performance estimator is structurally prevented from reading the labels it is scored against, enforced at the import graph by an import-linter contract and again by pytest.
claims.verification_note: type=forbidden, source_modules=['estimation'], forbidden_modules=['domains','backtest','reports']. The inline comment gives the reasoning: reaching a domain adapter would expose default_label_within_horizon and invalidate the evaluation. A second contract keeps drift_core domain-agnostic. Mirrored by tests/test_module_boundaries.py (153 lines).

claims.claim: A credit-default model frozen after training on 2013 H1 was backtested across 35 monthly windows covering 1,054,948 loans (2014-01 to 2016-11).
claims.source_location: README.md header; reports/backtest/signals.csv contains exactly 35 window rows
claims.verification_note: signals.csv row count is 35, window_id runs from 2014-01. Loan count stated in README and consistent with the 24-month fixed-horizon cut described there, under which 1,285,664 rows survive.

claims.claim: AUC held flat (0.6719 reference to 0.6661 final) while Brier rose 17% relative and the calibration gap widened 27-fold, so AUC-based monitoring would have reported nothing wrong.
claims.verification_note: Reference 2013 H2: AUC 0.6719, Brier 0.0916, gap -0.0019. 2016-11: AUC 0.6661, Brier 0.1069, gap -0.0259. Worst window 2015-12: gap -0.0513, which is the 27x figure against the -0.0019 reference. At that point the model under-stated portfolio default risk by about 36% relative. The base rate rose 19% while mean predicted risk fell slightly, which rules out the explanation that applicants simply became riskier.

claims.claim: No unsupervised signal gave genuine early warning: of six detectors, three (KS, Wasserstein, multivariate) fired on 100% of windows and prediction drift never fired at all.
claims.source_location: README.md results table; reports/backtest/signals.csv and latency.csv
claims.verification_note: Confirmed against signals.csv: ks_fired, wasserstein_fired and multivariate_fired are True on the first window and remain True; prediction_fired is False throughout. The README states that a detector firing on 100% of windows has maximum nominal lead time and zero information, and pre_onset_alert_rate exists in backtest/latency.py specifically to make that unquotable as a success.

claims.claim: The project publicly retracted its own headline finding after testing it: an originally reported anti-correlation (r = -0.38, p = 0.023) did not survive correction for serial dependence, and the corrected result is weaker.
claims.source_location: README.md section 2; HEAD commit message 'Retract the anti-correlated claim; it does not survive verification'
claims.verification_note: Three independent routes reported: effective n falls from 35 to 13.0, adjusted p = 0.195, moving-block bootstrap CI [-0.730, +0.280], and first differences flip the sign to r = +0.75. What survives is stated separately and is serial-correlation-robust: biased low in 35 of 35 windows (sign test p = 5.8e-11, still 2.4e-4 discounted to 13 effective observations), mean relative error -23.4%, Newey-West HAC slope on the gap +0.00096 per window (p = 0.0016). Reproducible via scripts/verify_correlation.py.

claims.claim: One bug pattern was found three times in code and twice more in the write-up: a safety check computed downstream of a transformation that removes the evidence the check looks for.
claims.verification_note: Three code instances: (1) permutation floor, only 15 permutations so the smallest achievable p of 0.0625 sat above alpha and AUC 1.0 was reported as no drift; (2) all-NaN KS, NaN-dropping ran before any validity check leaving an empty comparison returning statistic=nan, is_drifted=False; (3) ESS guardrail, weight clipping at the 99th percentile capped exactly the large weights ESS exists to detect, returning a confident base rate of 0.534 on windows six standard deviations apart. A fourth instance was in the prose, not the code. A fifth occurred inside the fix for the fourth and produced p = 0, a value no finite test can produce, pinned by test_non_integer_override_never_yields_p_equal_zero. The response was structural rather than three separate fixes: one shared contract in drift_core/validity.py, every result carries a status distinct from its severity, and is_drifted=False is never sufficient on its own.

claims.claim: Importance weighting, which is valid under covariate shift, answered only 4 of 35 windows and was still 19% low on those; the reference-vs-current discriminator AUC ran 0.897 to 0.9998, leaving no common support to reweight across.
claims.verification_note: The framing is the measured outcome rather than a caveat: correcting for everything observable about P(X) left the error essentially intact, because the error was in P(Y|X).

claims.claim: Measured false-positive rate against a synthetic null was 0.0% across 560 feature-window tests per method, which makes the constant firing on real data a property of the data rather than miscalibrated detectors.
claims.verification_note: Random splits of the healthy reference period. All four univariate detectors alerted zero times. The README reads this as making the result worse rather than better: the detectors are correctly calibrated and fire constantly because real credit populations never stop moving.

claims.claim: The design conclusion is that fixed-threshold alerting is the wrong architecture: the same statistics correlate with the true calibration gap (multivariate AUC r = 0.88, rising monotonically 0.636 to 0.803) but carry their signal in trajectory rather than level, so thresholding discards the informative part.
claims.verification_note: MANDATORY QUALIFIER carried by the source itself: these correlations are computed on autocorrelated series, are descriptive, are offered without p-values, and the same serial-dependence correction that sank r = -0.38 would widen their intervals substantially. The monotonicity of the multivariate AUC is presented as the more robust observation. The caveat must travel with the number.

claims.claim: The project states its own limits: there was no healthy deployment period to detect across (33 of 35 windows breach the Brier threshold), prediction drift's 'never fired' is threshold-dependent, the onset definition is contestable and is swept rather than chosen, and results rest on a single dataset and model class.
claims.verification_note: Latency is reported under four different ground-truth metrics and both free parameters of the onset rule are swept rather than chosen. Max PSI on the score distribution was 0.0894 against a 0.1 gate; at a 0.05 gate it fires on 11 of 35 windows and still would not have led the onset. Degradation began about two months after the training window ended, so the maximum achievable lead time was 2-4 windows regardless of detector quality.

claims.claim: ClinIQ analysed 52,184 patient-written drug reviews covering 2008-2017, of which 3,316 (6.4%) were SUD-relevant.
claims.verification_note: Row count confirmed programmatically. Source is the public Kaggle/UCI Drug Review dataset, not patient records. No PHI is involved.

claims.claim: Clustered 3,316 SUD-flagged reviews into 37 behavioural cohorts using UMAP and HDBSCAN over 384-dimensional all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings.
claims.verification_note: 38 unique values including HDBSCAN's -1 noise label, so 37 real cohorts. Embedding dimension 384 corroborated by db/schema.sql declaring embedding vector(384). IMPORTANT CAVEAT added 2026-10-01: sud_clusters.csv still holds 3,316 rows and was NOT regenerated after the proxy-label correction, so roughly 24% of the clustered reviews are now known to be false positives from the 'meth' substring bug. The 37 cohorts are therefore a result over a contaminated set. Re-running the clustering on the 2,513 corrected reviews would settle whether the structure survives. See cliniq.integrity.label_correction.

claims.claim: Patient distress proportion rose from 1.7% in 2008 to 30.5% in 2017 across the review corpus.
claims.source_location: outputs/temporal_trends.csv, which the repository now states predates the label fix
claims.verification_note: SUPERSEDED on 2026-09-29 and retained here so the record shows what changed. The SUD proxy label matched 'meth' as a SUBSTRING, so reviews of methylphenidate, sulfamethoxazole, methylprednisolone, dextromethorphan and indomethacin were counted as substance-use related. The repository states that 803 of 3,316 proxy-positive reviews, 24%, were positive only because of that. 'meth' is now required to be a whole word, pinned by test_meth_matches_only_as_a_whole_word. Recomputed on corrected labels the trend is 2.0% to 24.8%, not 1.7% to 30.5%, over 2,513 reviews rather than 3,316. The superseded figures must not be quoted. See cliniq.result.distress_trend_corrected.

claims.claim: ClinIQ compares three retrieval tiers on the same labelled task: rule-based, embedding cosine similarity, and Claude plus pgvector RAG.
claims.verification_note: A genuine baseline ladder over a shared evaluation set, not three unrelated demos. pgvector confirmed at db/schema.sql line 1 (CREATE EXTENSION vector) and line 47 (embedding vector(384)). Anthropic SDK confirmed at agent/cliniq_agent.py line 8; the API key is read from the environment, not hardcoded.

claims.claim: The three tiers trade off sharply against each other: rule-based reached precision 0.861 and recall 0.847, embedding reached precision 0.504 and recall 1.000, and LLM plus RAG reached precision 0.938 and recall 0.400.
claims.verification_note: Exact committed values: rule_based 0.8610169491525423 / 0.8466666666666667 (tp 254, fp 41, fn 46, tn 259); embedding 0.5042016806722689 / 1.0 (tp 300, fp 295, fn 0, tn 5); llm_rag 0.9375 / 0.4 (tp 120, fp 8, fn 180, tn 292). Elapsed time spans three orders of magnitude: 0.05s, 9.3s, 1772.7s. CRITICAL: no single tier achieved both high precision and perfect recall. See CONFLICTS.md entry C-001. CAVEAT added 2026-10-01: the CSV is byte-identical at the new commit, so these numbers are unchanged, but the repository now states they were scored against the OLD labels and were not rerun after the correction, because doing so needs the database and a paid API. Re-run offline on corrected labels the rules baseline scores F1 0.846 rather than 0.854. Treat these as the original team benchmark rather than the current best estimate.

claims.claim: The pipeline identified 219 SUD documentation gaps carrying $537,340.22 of revenue at risk, computed from CMS FY2024 IPPS Final Rule DRG weights.
claims.verification_note: MANDATORY QUALIFIER: the same summary block states 'Synthetic claims analyzed: 220 (all fictional)'. The dollar figure is a modelled result over fictional claims demonstrating that the DRG-weight calculation works, not revenue identified in a real payer population. Any presentation omitting the word synthetic misrepresents it. See CONFLICTS.md entry C-002.

claims.claim: Every ClinIQ output is grounded in a cited government source, with source_url stored per embedding so each answer is auditable back to its document.
claims.verification_note: The schema comment reads 'source_url field makes every embedding fully auditable'. The knowledge base is 122 embeddings over 10 registered source documents: 30 DRG-weight chunks from CMS FY2024 IPPS Final Rule Table 5, 32 ICD-10 chunks from the FY2024 official code set, and 60 SUD-signal chunks. pipeline_summary.txt confirms 'Every output cites RAG source: YES'.

claims.claim: ClinIQ was built for the NSF NRT Research-A-Thon 2026 (4th place, self-reported) and later extended with FHIR interoperability, a prior-authorization agent, an active-learning labelling workbench and a counterfactual bias test. The repository is public on this account.
claims.verification_note: Built together as a team project. The README at the pinned commit documents each extension with its evaluation results.

claims.source_location: Repository description; LinkedIn post with event poster
claims.verification_note: No organiser-published results page was located during verification. Presented as self-reported until an organiser result is linked.

claims.claim: A fine-tuned BERT churn classifier reached 0.793 accuracy and macro F1 0.73 on 1,409 held-out customers.
claims.verification_note: The exact value in the committed notebook output is 0.7927608232789212, with the sklearn classification report showing macro avg 0.73 over support 1409. A second, weaker run at 0.77 accuracy and macro avg 0.68 is also present in the same notebook; the reported figure is the stronger of the two and that should be said if asked.

claims.claim: T5 was chained after the classifier to convert structured customer rows into plain-language risk narratives, and SHAP over XGBoost ranked the churn drivers as contract type, tenure and monthly charges.
claims.verification_note: 1.7 MB of generated summaries are committed as an artifact rather than only described, so the model output is directly inspectable.

claims.claim: Stable Diffusion 1.5's CLIP text encoder was replaced with a custom KinematicEncoder mapping 76-dimensional robot kinematics into cross-attention, fine-tuned with LoRA rank 4 via peft.
claims.verification_note: Verified in the fork's code: 76-dim input, MLP 256/512, producing 77x768 tokens, plus a gesture nn.Embedding(16,768) and LayerNorm. LoRA rank 4 applied to to_q, to_k, to_v and to_out.0 via peft. DDPM training, DDIM sampling, 256px, batch 4, 50 epochs, frame_stride 90, checkpoint step_1480. JIGSAWS Suturing loader uses OneTrialOut folds with StandardScaler and lazy OpenCV seeking.

claims.claim: Generation quality was evaluated against a cross-pair baseline in which each generated frame is also scored against a different real frame, separating genuine conditioning from scene-average reconstruction.
claims.verification_note: metrics_on_grid.py computes PSNR, SSIM, histogram chi-squared and edge IoU with a diagonal-versus-off-diagonal comparison. video_quality_metrics.py computes per-frame SSIM, Farneback optical-flow correlation and MAD flicker flags. The baseline design is the methodologically interesting part and it is real in the code. LIMITATION: it was run over only 4 pairs from a smoke test, which is too few to support a strong quantitative claim.

claims.claim: Generated frames scored PSNR 19-22 dB and SSIM 0.61-0.74 against a VAE reconstruction ceiling of 24-27 dB and 0.82-0.91.
claims.source_location: SS-SD_Report_4pg.pdf (team report, May 2026), held locally and not published in the repository
claims.verification_note: No metric values are committed in either the fork or upstream, so these numbers cannot be reproduced from the public repository, and this claim therefore carries NO code link: linking metrics_on_grid.py here would imply the script evidences these figures, which it does not. The script's existence is a separate, VERIFIED claim (see sssd.eval.cross_pair_baseline). The stated basis for the numbers is a 12-sample held-out expert grid at checkpoint step_1480 in a team report held privately. Committing reports/metrics.json would move this to VERIFIED in one commit.

claims.claim: FID was used to benchmark generated surgical video.
claims.source_location: scripts/compute_fid.py, present in the fork since the upstream sync (commit b5b2cb8)
claims.verification_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-28. An earlier review recorded this as UNSUPPORTED on the basis that compute_fid.py existed only upstream. That was wrong: the script is present in the fork, and has been since the 21 Sept 2026 upstream sync. What is still absent is any FID VALUE. A repository-wide search for committed metric values returns nothing, in any JSON or CSV, for FID, PSNR or SSIM. So the tooling is real and the result is not published. The claim is therefore self-reported rather than unsupported, and carries no code link, because linking the script would imply it evidences a number it has never been shown to produce. Running it and committing the output would move this to VERIFIED. See CONFLICTS.md C-003.

claims.claim: SS-SD is a team capstone. The repository on this account is a fork; upstream commits are the teammate's.
claims.verification_note: The fork was synced with upstream on 2026-09-21 and is current rather than a stale snapshot. 33 tests in the fork: 30 pass, 3 fail on Windows only, due to a NamedTemporaryFile unlink issue in test_jigsaws_metafile.py. Five scripts hard-code a teammate's local paths, notebooks 01-04 are empty stubs, and ControlNet is a todo scaffold. None of that is hidden.
